source.title: Tighter risk certificates for neural networks
source.authors: M. Pérez-Ortiz; Omar Rivasplata; J. Shawe-Taylor; Csaba Szepesvari

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper; no material garbling or cutoff is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares test errors across fully connected and convolutional probabilistic networks trained with PAC-Bayes objectives, a different training method from the version’s stated standard-training setup.
record.gate_note: Only V3 is tested. The paper reports no random-label experiments, width sweep beyond interpolation, optimizer or batch-size comparison, dropout effect on the posterior, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Figure 2 varies fully connected architecture size, but reports risk certificates and test error without testing interpolation-threshold behavior.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares MNIST test errors of convolutional and fully connected networks under matched probabilistic training objectives, bearing on V3 through a different training method. Table 1 also includes a standard ERM architecture comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate: PBB produces competitive test errors and tighter non-vacuous risk certificates on MNIST and CIFAR-10, and the tested MNIST CNN improves performance and certificates over the FCN. The authors describe self-certified learning as promising, while explicitly requiring broader empirical or theoretical validation before claiming it achieved.
record.recipe_differences: Probabilistic networks trained by PAC-Bayes-derived objectives and vanilla SGD with momentum; the architecture comparison is not the original fixed-weight standard-training setup.
record.method_sensitivity: On MNIST, test errors and risk certificates vary with objective and prior choice; the reported CNN-versus-FCN test-error ordering is consistent across the listed settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Figures 1 and 2 associate PAC-Bayes risk certificates with test error across hyperparameters and architectures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: PAC-Bayes risk certificates can help rank predictors for model selection; this does not establish V7's magnitude-aware sharpness relationship.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the test errors. The architecture comparison concerns only one MNIST FCN/CNN pair in probabilistic networks and does not isolate local connectivity or test the broader stated conditions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows beyond the MNIST stochastic-predictor architecture comparisons were extracted. CIFAR-10 results compare CNN objectives and sizes, but do not compare convolutional with fully connected networks.

untested.parts: Fitting fixed random labels and comparing natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Widening beyond the zero-training-error threshold; Figure 2 does not establish this threshold or the required width-dependent test-error trend.
The causal contribution of local connectivity, learning sparse local connections, initialization from trained convolutional networks, and architecture comparisons on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and SVHN.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, tuning-budget dependence, optimizer switching and decoupled weight decay.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove a batch-size penalty.

A reported dropout-versus-no-dropout held-out error comparison, small-data dependence, excessive dropout and joint removal with weight decay. Dropout is used and tuned for prior learning, but its effect is not separately reported.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based rankings.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing an equal number of random examples and retraining.

missing.what: Add the standard ERM MNIST architecture comparison: deterministic test error is 0.0092 for CNN and 0.0152 for FCN. This directly addresses V3's standard gradient-training setting, which the record incorrectly treats as entirely untested here.

record.verdict_notes: R1–R8 and R9–R16 represent eight paired comparisons, not sixteen independent results. The architecture comparison does not isolate connectivity from depth or other architectural differences. The study is not an original source for V3.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width beyond the zero-training-error threshold and its effect on test error.
The comparison is limited to probabilistic MNIST networks trained with the paper’s PAC-Bayes objectives; local connectivity and the other listed datasets and initialization methods are not tested.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and their held-out performance.
Large versus small batch sizes and recipe adaptations.
Dropout’s effect on held-out error of the trained classifier; dropout is used only while learning priors in the experiments.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness and its relationship to the train-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
